title: Inaugural meeting swears in new Council
subtitle: Mayor's inaugural address outlines priorities: housing, growth, infrastructure, short-term rentals, parking, water protection and climate adaptation.
overview: Centre Wellington's 2022-2026 Council held its inaugural meeting. Six ward councillors and the mayor took their declarations of office, and Mayor Shawn Watters received the chain of office. The evening also included a piper, a land acknowledgement and the singing of O Canada.

The minutes record no motions, so no formal decisions were made. The main business was the mayor's inaugural address, which set out the challenges the new Council expects to face. These include managing growth targets and an attainable housing strategy, cost-effective roads and bridges, budgets in challenging times, and short-term rental and downtown parking strategies.

The mayor also listed protecting water and farmland, a climate adaptation strategy, preserving cultural heritage, and building a welcoming community and an accountable Council. Residents were asked to be patient while the new Council settles in. Relationships with First Nations, the County of Wellington and the Province were called important partnerships. The meeting adjourned, and attendees were invited to a reception downstairs.
